paragraphs.text: Exordium simplicissimum, saith Junius. A very plain preface calling for attention; (1.) From the authority of the speaker; (2.) From the duty of the hearers.
paragraphs.anchor: Hear ye the word which the Lord speaketh.

paragraphs.text: The ten tribes, long since captivated, and now directed what to do, say some; the Jews, say others: and in this former part of the chapter, those of them that had been carried away to Babylon with Jeconiah.
paragraphs.anchor: O house of Israel.

paragraphs.text: Their sinful customs and irregular religions - mere irreligious. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Learn not the way of the heathen.

paragraphs.text: Which the blind heathens feared and deified; and none did more than the Syrians, the Jews’ next neighbours. Of the vanity of judicial astrology, see on Isa 47:13. He who feareth God needs not fear the stars; for "all things are yours," saith the apostle. {1Co 3:21} Mulcasses, King of Tunis, a great star gazer, foreseeing by them, as he said, the loss of his kingdom and life together, left Africa that he might shun that mischief; but thereby he hastened it, A.D. 1544. God suffereth sometimes such fond predictions to fall out right upon men for a just punishment of their curiosity.
paragraphs.anchor: And be not dismayed at the signs of heaven.

paragraphs.text: Therefore God’s people should not, if it were for no other reason but that only. See Mat 6:32. Let Papists observe this.
paragraphs.anchor: For the heathen are dismayed at them.

paragraphs.text: {a} See Selden. De Diis Syris.
For the customs of the people {a} are vain.] Their rites confirmed by custom; their imagery, for instance, a very magnum nihil, whether ye look to the efficient matter, form, or end of those idols.
See Isa 40:2; Isa 44:12-17, which last place Jeremiah here seemeth to have imitated.
paragraphs.anchor: For one cutteth a tree out of the forest.

paragraphs.text: {a} Caeremoniae populorum,
Gild it over to make it sightly; goodly gods there while. See Isa 4:4.
paragraphs.anchor: They deck it with silver and with gold.

paragraphs.text: Ut non amittat, saith Tremellius: that it lose not the cost bestowed upon it.
paragraphs.anchor: That it move not.

paragraphs.text: Which is straight, tall, smooth, and in summo profert fructus, and beareth fruits at the very top of it.
paragraphs.anchor: They are upright as the palm tree.

paragraphs.text: None of all these dii minutuli, these dunghill deities, are worthy to be named in the same day with thee.
paragraphs.anchor: Forasmuch as there is none like unto thee.

paragraphs.text: God is great; {Psa 77:13} greater; {Job 33:12} greatest; {Psa 95:3} greatness itself. {Psa 145:3} He is a degree above the superlative. Think the same of other his names and attributes, many of which we have here mentioned in this and the following verses; which are therefore highly to be prized, and oft to be perused. Leonard Lessius, a little before his death, finished his book concerning the fifty names of almighty God; often affirming, that in that little book he had found more light and spiritual support under those grievous fits of the stone which he suffered, than in all his voluminous commentaries upon Aquinas’s sums, which he had well nigh fitted for the press. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Thou art great.

paragraphs.text: {a} Ex Vita Lessii.
Tremble at thy transcendent greatness, thy matchless majesty, power, and prowess? See Mal 1:14 Rev 15:4 Psa 103:19. {See Trapp on "Mal 1:14"} {See Trapp on "Rev 15:4"} {See Trapp on "Psa 103:19"}
paragraphs.anchor: Who would not fear thee, O King of nations?

paragraphs.text: Who used to deify their wise men and their kings.
paragraphs.anchor: Forasmuch as among all the wise men of the nations.

paragraphs.text: The wise men are, for that, when they knew there was but one only true God - as did Pythagoras, Socrates, Plato, Seneca, &c. - they "detained the truth in unrighteousness," and taught the people to worship stocks and stones. {Rom 1:21-23} The nations are, because they yield to be taught devotion by images under what pretext soever. Considerentur hic subterfugia Papistarum. Let them regard this strategm of Popery. Pope Gregory first taught that images in churches were laymen’s books, a doctrine of devils.
paragraphs.anchor: But they are altogether brutish and foolish.

paragraphs.text: See Isa 40:19.
paragraphs.anchor: Silver spread into plates.

paragraphs.text: From Tarsus or Tartessus; {Eze 27:12} from Africa, saith the Chaldee. Idolaters spare for no cost.
paragraphs.anchor: Is brought from Tarshish.

paragraphs.text: The same with Phaz; {Job 28:17} or with Ophir, as some; Aurum Obzyrum.
paragraphs.anchor: And gold from Uphaz.

paragraphs.text: Quaerunt suos Phidias et Praxiteles: but how could those give that deity which themselves had not?
paragraphs.anchor: They are all the work of cunning men.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Jehovah is God in truth, not in conceit only, or counterfeit.
paragraphs.anchor: But the Lord is the true God.

paragraphs.text: See on Jer 10:6. The words are in the plural number, "he is the living Gods"; not for the sake of honour and glory, as Kimchi observes; but as denoting a trinity of Persons in the unity of the divine essence: for though the words àìäéí ηιιν, "living Gods," that is, living divine Ones, or Persons, are in the plural number, yet äåà, "he," is in the singular; which is worthy of observation. {Hebrew Text Note}
paragraphs.anchor: He is the living God, and an everlasting king.

paragraphs.text: At his wrath the earth shall tremble.] The earth, that greatest of all lifeless creatures.
And the nations shall not be able.] Less able to stand before him than a glass bottle before a cannon shot.

Confession with the mouth is necessary to salvation. This verse (written therefore in the Syriac tongue, which was spoken at Babylon) is a formulary given to God’s people, to be made use of by them in detestation of the idolatries of that city.
paragraphs.anchor: Thus shall ye say unto them.

paragraphs.text: The vanity of idols and heathenish gods is set forth (1.) By their impotence; (2.) Frailty. Quid ad haec respondebunt Papistae? aut qualem contradictoriae reconciliationem afferent?
paragraphs.anchor: The gods that made not the heaven and the earth.

paragraphs.text: Here we have the true philosophy and right origin of things: Felix qui potuit rerum cognoscere causas. Almighty God made the earth, the main bulk and body of it. {Gen 1:1} He alone is the powerful Creator, the provident Disposer, the prudent Preserver of all things both in heaven and in earth; therefore the only true God.
paragraphs.anchor: He hath made the earth by his power.

paragraphs.text: Again, when he thundereth, {Psa 29:3} it raineth amain, lightneth in the midst of the rain (which is a great miracle), and bloweth for life, as we say, no man knowing whence or whither. {Joh 3:8} All which wondrous works of God may well serve for a theological alphabet, and cannot be attributed to any god but our God.
paragraphs.anchor: When he uttereth his voice.

paragraphs.text: See Psa 135:7. {See Trapp on "Psa 135:7"}
paragraphs.anchor: And he causeth the vapours to ascend.

paragraphs.text: Or, Every man is become more brutish than to know. That was therefore a hyperbolical praise given by Philostratus to Apollonius, Non doctus sed natus sapiens, that he was not taught, but born a wise man. See Job 11:12 Rom 1:22. {See Trapp on "Job 11:12"} {See Trapp on "Rom 1:22"} Every man is become brutish for want of knowledge (so the words may be rendered), the heathen idol makers especially; Brutescit homo prae scientia, so Vatablus. Every man is brutish, in comparison of knowledge, viz., of God’s knowledge, while he goeth about to search into the causes of rain, lightning, wind, &c., which God only understandeth.
paragraphs.anchor: Every man is brutish in his knowledge.

paragraphs.text: Vanity, in its largest extent, is properly predicated of them.
paragraphs.anchor: They are vanity.

paragraphs.text: Mere mockeries, making men to embrace vanity for verity.
paragraphs.anchor: And the work of errors.

paragraphs.text: See on Isa 46:1.
paragraphs.anchor: In the time of their visitation.

paragraphs.text: God is his people’s "portion"; they are his "possession." Oh their dignity and security! This the cock on the dunghill understands not.
paragraphs.anchor: The Portion of Jacob is not like them.

paragraphs.text: Make up thy pack, and prevent a plundering. Reculas tuas et sarcinas compone.
paragraphs.anchor: Gather up thy wares out of the land.

paragraphs.text: I will easily and speedily sling them, and sling them into Babylon; so God will one day hurl into hell all the wicked of the earth. {Psa 9:17}
paragraphs.anchor: BehoId, I will sling out the inhabitants of this land.

paragraphs.text: Just so as they were foretold it would be, but they could never be drawn to believe it.
paragraphs.anchor: And will distress them, that they may find it so.

paragraphs.text: This is the moan that people make when in distress, and they find it so. But what after a while of paining?
paragraphs.anchor: Woe is me for my hurt! my wound is grievous.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Bear it off, as well as I may, by head and shoulders, or bear up under it, and rub through it, wearing it out as well as I can; when things are at worst, they mend again. Crosses, as they had a time to come in, so they must have a time to go out, &c. This is not patience, but pertinace, the "strength of stones and flesh of brass"; {Job 6:12} it draweth on more weight of plagues and punishments. God liketh not this indolence, this stupidity, this despising of his corrections, as he calleth it; {Heb 12:5} such shall be made to cry, when God bindeth them, {Job 36:11} as here.
paragraphs.anchor: Truly this is my grief, and I must bear it

paragraphs.text: I am irreparably ruined; like as when a camp is quite broken up, not any part of a tent or hut is left standing.
paragraphs.anchor: My tabernacle is spoiled.

paragraphs.text: The corrupt prophets and priests, who seduced the people from the truth, were persons that made no conscience of prayer; hence all went to wrack and ruin.
paragraphs.anchor: For the pastors are become brutish.

paragraphs.text: This doleful peal he oft rung in their ears, but they little regarded it. See Jer 9:11.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, the noise of the bruit is come.

paragraphs.text: He is not master of his own way, but is directed and overruled by the powerful providence; even this cruel Chaldean also, that marcheth against us.
paragraphs.anchor: O Lord, I know that the way of man is not in himself.

paragraphs.text: We know not what to do, or which way to turn ourselves, only our eyes are toward thee. Behold, we submit to thy justice, and implore thy mercy. This text doth mainly make against freewill, saith Oecolampadius; and yet the Pelagians would hence gather that man can, by his own strength, walk in the way to heaven; but he must be helped, say they, by God’s grace, that he may be perfect.
paragraphs.anchor: It is not in man that walketh to direct his steps.

paragraphs.text: {a} i.e., In mercy and in measure. Correction is not simply to be deprecated; the prophet here cries, Correct me; David saith, It was good for me. Job calleth God’s afflicting of us his magnifying of us. {Jer 7:17} Feri Domine, feri clementer; ipse paratus sum, saith Luther, - Smite, Lord, smite me, but gently, and I am ready to bear it patiently. King Alfred prayed God to send him always some sickness, whereby his body might be tamed, and he the better disposed and affectioned to Godward. Ecclesiastical history telleth of one Servulus, who, sick of a palsy, so that his life was a lingering death, said ordinarily, God be thanked.
paragraphs.anchor: O Lord, correct me; but with judgment

paragraphs.text: {a} Cum ratione seu modo. Leniter et discrete. - A Lap.
This is not more votum, than vaticinium; a prayer, than a prophecy.
paragraphs.anchor: Pour out, &c.

paragraphs.text: Neglect of family prayer uncovers the roof, as it were, for God’s curse to be rained down upon men’s tables, meals, enterprises, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: And upon the families.
